gaps.sentence: 'We're moving to Lisbon,' they announced. They announced that they ___ to Lisbon.
gaps.explanation: Present continuous backshifts to past continuous: are moving → were moving.

gaps.sentence: She ___ me not to worry about the deadline.
gaps.hint: tell sb not to do sth
gaps.explanation: Only 'tell' takes a personal object + not to + infinitive; 'said me not to' is impossible.

gaps.sentence: 'Why did you cancel the order?' he asked. He asked why I ___ the order.
gaps.explanation: Wh-questions keep the wh-word but drop do-support and backshift: did you cancel → I had cancelled.

gaps.sentence: 'I must finish this today,' she said. She said she ___ finish it that day.
gaps.explanation: Must expressing obligation usually becomes had to in reported speech; 'today' becomes 'that day'.

gaps.sentence: 'We're leaving here at dawn,' they said. They said they were leaving ___ at dawn.
gaps.explanation: Place adverbs shift with the speaker's perspective: here → there.

gaps.sentence: 'Come round to my house tomorrow,' she said. She invited me round to her house ___.
gaps.explanation: Tomorrow becomes the next day (the following day) when the invitation is reported.

gaps.sentence: He ___ me that the meeting had been cancelled.
gaps.explanation: 'Tell' takes a personal object (told me); 'said me' is wrong, and speak/talk don't take that-clauses.

gaps.sentence: 'I saw the accident happen,' the witness stated. The witness stated that he ___ the accident happen.
gaps.explanation: Past simple backshifts to past perfect after a past reporting verb: saw → had seen.
